reason: E1 shows oxidation resistance and low wear for an HEA film at 800 °C, E2 studies hot corrosion of laser-cladded HEA coatings at 900 °C in molten salt, and E3 demonstrates reduced wear and high hardness for a laser-cladded HEA composite. However, E1 uses a different deposition method and composition, E2 does not report wear or hardness outcomes, and E3 does not test high-temperature or corrosive conditions, so the combined evidence only partly supports the specific combination of properties claimed.
premises: Laser-cladded HEA coatings can form dense, metallurgically bonded microstructures with high hardness
HEA coatings can form protective oxide layers (e.g., composite oxides) at high temperatures that reduce oxidation
HEA coatings can exhibit significantly lower wear rates compared to uncoated substrates
HEA coatings can withstand aggressive environments up to 800–900 °C, including molten salt corrosion
